name: tool-usage-integration-registry
purpose: Captures high-signal Codex-style tool usage loops so the desktop platform can expose them as reusable agent work playbooks, validation ladders, and source-linked implementation targets.

reader_guide.summary: Use this registry when turning repeated agent tool behavior into desktop product behavior, Tool Studio guidance, validation commands, or future automation.
how_to_read: Read patterns first to see the human-readable work sequence and the tool surfaces involved.
Read verification_ladders to see which commands or checks prove a pattern is usable in the platform.
Read adoption_backlog before adding new source, because it names the next bounded platform surfaces for these tool loops.
Keep new entries narrow: each pattern should describe one repeatable tool loop with evidence outputs and failure modes.
update_triggers: A repeated Codex or agent tool workflow appears in multiple meaningful tasks.
A new desktop surface should teach, run, or validate a tool sequence directly.
Tool use changes from ad hoc terminal use into a platform-owned capability.
Validation, build, package, or resource cleanup behavior changes.

reference_links.title: Playwright Locators
used_for: prefer user-perceived locators for browser smoke checks
reference_links.limitations: Applies to browser automation; native shell validation still needs OS/runtime checks.

reference_links.title: Node.js Test Runner
used_for: repository-local smoke and contract tests with node --test
fast no-extra-framework validation for monitor collectors and source audits
reference_links.limitations: Does not replace browser, Tauri, or Rust runtime checks.

reference_links.title: Tauri Distribute
reference_links.limitations: Public macOS readiness still requires signing, hardened runtime, notarization, and installer policy gates.

structure_rules.rule: Repeated agent tool usage shall become a platform-visible playbook before it becomes opaque automation.
structure_rules.reason: The user asked to bring the tool usage style itself into the platform, not just ship a one-off fix.

structure_rules.rule: Research, local inspection, source edits, validation, packaging, and git close-out must each leave evidence outputs before a task is considered done.
structure_rules.reason: The platform needs durable trust handles for long-running agent work.

structure_rules.rule: Tool playbooks that touch servers, browser automation, subprocesses, caches, memory, or packaging must include lifecycle and cleanup checks.
structure_rules.reason: The platform is a desktop app and should own resource lifecycle instead of behaving like a stateless page.

field_guide.meaning: Repeatable tool-use loops that a platform agent or human operator can follow.
Grouped validation commands and acceptance checks mapped to platform surfaces.
Bounded future platform source targets for making each loop more executable.

patterns.label: Web-first research
patterns.purpose: Confirm unstable or tool-specific facts with current primary sources before planning, editing, or claiming readiness.
trigger_when: The user asks for latest, current, best practice, open-source references, packaging, API behavior, or broad platform design.
A task depends on a page, repository, library, or documentation not already loaded into context.
sequence: Search high-authority sources first.
Prefer official docs for implementation behavior.
Record queries, checked sources, weak sources ignored, plan impact, and uncertainty.
Only carry source claims into implementation when the source changes the plan or risk model.
failure_modes: Using stale model memory for changed library behavior.
Treating community signals as factual proof.
Forgetting to carry source uncertainty into the plan.
patterns.platform_application: Tool Studio should show research as a first gate for tool creation, validation, packaging, and external integration work.

patterns.label: Parallel local inspection
patterns.purpose: Read existing source, tests, configs, and docs quickly without flooding the operator with noisy shell output.
trigger_when: The task needs repo context across source, UI, tests, configs, and docs.
Multiple read-only inspections can run without touching shared mutable state.
sequence: Start with git status and targeted file maps.
Use rg for text and file discovery.
Read related source files in parallel when they are independent.
Summarize the system shape before editing.
failure_modes: Reading too much source by default.
Running parallel commands that mutate the same file or git state.
Chaining shell output into unreadable logs.
patterns.platform_application: A future desktop source-intake lane can precompute read-only maps and expose them beside the code editor.

patterns.label: Snapshot worker thread pool
patterns.purpose: Use multiple Node worker threads for independent document rendering and source preview work during startup snapshot collection.
trigger_when: The monitor must transform hundreds or thousands of independent documents.
Source previews can be read independently and sorted after processing.
Startup snapshot collection becomes a visible boot-time cost.
sequence: Collect document and source-file tasks without reading every payload.
Choose worker count from available CPU parallelism and task count.
Run document rendering and source preview extraction through a bounded worker pool.
Fall back to the previous synchronous path if worker startup or execution fails.
Record worker counts in the generated snapshot stats.
evidence_outputs: collect timing with CPU utilization above one core
failure_modes: Spawning too many workers and making small repositories slower.
Assuming worker parallelism helps network or UI-bound work.
Dropping deterministic sorting after parallel task completion.
patterns.platform_application: Workspace Monitor startup collection now uses CPU-aware worker parallelism while preserving deterministic snapshots and synchronous fallback.

patterns.label: Patch-based editing
patterns.purpose: Make scoped source changes with reviewable diffs while preserving user work and avoiding destructive operations.
trigger_when: A source, config, test, or document change is needed.
The worktree may include user changes that must not be reverted.
sequence: Announce the edit target and intent.
Apply the smallest coherent patch.
Inspect the diff after edits.
Avoid reset, checkout, or deletion unless the user explicitly requested it.
failure_modes: Overwriting unrelated user edits.
Refactoring beyond the requested behavioral surface.
Editing generated files before the source of truth.
patterns.platform_application: Source workbench should support patch queues, diff preview, and protected user-change boundaries.

patterns.label: Renderer validation loop
patterns.purpose: Validate TypeScript, collector contracts, static UI rules, browser rendering, and performance-sensitive surfaces before packaging.
trigger_when: Workspace Monitor source, snapshot schema, UI, CSS, or generated data changes.
A user-reported interaction or rendering problem is being fixed.
sequence: Regenerate the workspace snapshot.
Run TypeScript and source contract checks.
Run node --test suites.
Open the relevant UI route with a browser smoke check.
Check visible text, stable controls, and nonblank surfaces.
failure_modes: Passing static tests while the UI route is blank.
Updating UI without the snapshot schema.
Forgetting to regenerate developer snapshot after customer packaging.
patterns.platform_application: Tool Studio should expose the renderer validation ladder directly beside build and deployment controls.

patterns.label: Desktop packaging loop
patterns.purpose: Turn a verified renderer and Tauri shell into local macOS artifacts without making the user run build steps manually.
trigger_when: The user asks for runnable desktop app changes.
Renderer, Tauri command, native process, packaging, or installer-adjacent behavior changes.
sequence: Prepare the renderer snapshot and static output.
Run the internal desktop packaging command.
Verify .app and DMG artifact paths.
Record public-readiness gaps separately from local internal readiness.
failure_modes: Claiming public macOS readiness without notarization and hardened-runtime gates.
Leaving customer snapshot in place after internal packaging.
Treating a web build as enough for desktop runtime changes.
patterns.platform_application: Desktop Runtime and Tool Studio should show packaging as a first-class validation ladder, not an afterthought.

patterns.label: Resource cleanup loop
patterns.purpose: Prevent leaking dev servers, browser sessions, PTYs, subprocess pipes, timers, caches, or native runtime handles.
trigger_when: The task starts a server, browser automation, terminal session, subprocess, worker, queue, stream, timer, or native resource.
A desktop optimization touches CPU, RAM, PTY, pipes, or cache behavior.
sequence: Name every long-running resource before starting it.
Attach a stop, close, or dispose action.
Confirm cleanup before final response.
Record residual resource risk when cleanup cannot be proven.
failure_modes: Leaving dev servers running after verification.
Keeping stale browser tabs or PTY sessions alive.
Holding file handles or pipes across task boundaries.
patterns.platform_application: Native runtime panels should expose process and pipe lifecycle state as part of task health.

patterns.label: Git close-out loop
patterns.purpose: Turn a completed change set into an auditable commit and push only after validation and final evaluation records exist.
trigger_when: A meaningful source, config, documentation, or history change is complete.
Repository rules require commit and push for completed work.
sequence: Review the diff and changed paths.
Run required validation and package steps.
Write work summary, evaluation, omission check, and trace records.
Commit with a scoped conventional message.
Push to origin/main unless explicitly told not to.
failure_modes: Committing before validation artifacts exist.
Bundling unrelated user changes.
Leaving the user to run the final build.
patterns.platform_application: The platform should make finalization explicit: evidence, validation, commit, push, and artifact paths.

verification_ladders.label: Workspace Monitor source ladder
acceptance: Tool Studio renders the Agent Tool Playbook.
Static tests cover collector, UI, and snapshot type contracts.

verification_ladders.label: Parallel snapshot ladder
acceptance: snapshotDocumentWorkers is greater than one on multi-core developer machines with enough documents.
snapshotSourceWorkers is greater than one when enough source candidates exist.
Generated documents and source files remain deterministic after parallel processing.

verification_ladders.label: Desktop package ladder
acceptance: Internal .app and DMG artifacts are generated.
Public-readiness caveats remain separate from internal runnable artifacts.
Developer snapshot is restored after customer bundle generation when needed.

verification_ladders.label: Runtime resource ladder
acceptance: Dev servers and browser sessions started by the task are stopped.
Long-running processes are named and have cleanup actions.
Residual risk is recorded when cleanup cannot be proven.

adoption_backlog.title: Turn playbook entries into executable task presets
risk_controls: Install and external mutation steps require explicit approval.
Every preset records evidence and rollback.

adoption_backlog.title: Persist tool-call traces and validation ladders per task run
risk_controls: Keep raw logs separate from operator summaries.
